what: Effective-n gate: granularity-bearing pairs PER SPLIT x e-0040 McNemar power. Only granularity-bearing test pairs can express a granularity (not format) effect, so they -- not n=63 -- set the effective sample size for the headline q-0007/q-0001 claim.

mde.note: nominal column = the term-vs-tactic FORMAT effect e-0040 priced at n=63; effective column = the GRANULARITY effect, the project's actual headline, at n_eff.

interpretation: The held-out test split has 63 pairs but only 5 are granularity-bearing (3 with a >=2 frontier). McNemar's exact two-sided test needs >=6 same-direction discordant pairs to reach alpha=0.05; with at most 5 granularity-bearing problems the discordant ceiling is 5 < 6, so the test CANNOT reject under ANY effect size -- power is exactly 0, not merely low. The n=63 MDE the power quartet reported prices the term-vs-tactic FORMAT effect, not the granularity effect the paper claims. To make the granularity effect even POSSIBLE to resolve, the eval must draw its held-out set from granularity-bearing decls (the data/deep route) -- corpus_v3's split cannot do it.
